speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms in detail, specifically regarding the timing and triggers of your shooting ear pain and your difficulty wearing earrings following your tympanoplasty.

To better assess your current ear health, would you be willing to undergo an examination to check for scarring, retraction, or granulation tissue?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. The timing of your shooting pain while eating is highly suggestive of neuralgia involving the auriculotemporal nerve. To evaluate the surgical site for potential causes like cholesteatoma or granulation tissue, I will request an Otoscopic exam.

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The right ear canal is clear. The tympanic membrane appears intact with no evidence of cholesteatoma, granulation tissue, or perforation. The surgical site shows expected healing without active infection.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The shooting pain triggered by eating strongly suggests auriculotemporal nerve entrapment or neuralgia following your tympanoplasty. To confirm this and rule out other surgical complications, I need to see the operative site.

REQUEST IMAGES: Post-tympanoplasty Otoscopic Images

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia secondary to Tympanoplasty.
